framework: China - Provisions on Deep Synthesis (in force 10 Jan 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers with public opinion or mobilisation capacity must file under the algorithm recommendation provisions; technical supporters file by reference; filed entities must display the filing number and link.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
clause_or_page: EC AI Act policy page, 'Application timeline' paragraph
requirement_paraphrase: Commission page states the Act became applicable on 2 August 2026 with exceptions: prohibitions and AI literacy from 2 Feb 2025; governance and GPAI obligations from 2 Aug 2025; Annex I high-risk to 2 Aug 2028; Annex III to 2 Dec 2027; AI Omnibus political agreement 7 May 2026, in force 27 July 2026.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems conforming to harmonised standards (or parts) whose references are published in the OJ are presumed to meet the Section 2 requirements to the extent the standards cover them.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing requires a testing plan submitted to the market surveillance authority and approved (tacitly after 30 days unless national law requires authorisation), registration with a unique EU identification number, and a duration of at most six months extendable by six more.
what_is_tested: Authorisation and registration of real-world tests

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.
what_is_tested: Pre-market and periodic testing of AI-content marking and detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.
what_is_tested: Security assurance testing of model and infrastructure
who_tests: Signatory provider; independent external security reviewers

framework: Japan - AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Government is to develop guidelines and other measures in line with international norms to ensure appropriate AI R&D and use.

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The v2.0 decision takes effect on 1 Sep 2026; CAIO measures under Sec. 6.2 were to be set by 30 Jun 2026 and the AI governance framework scope under Sec. 2.2.2 applies from 1 Jul 2026.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 2, Deploy and Monitor item 3, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: The AI system should be tested to ensure the combination of available data does not reveal sensitive data or break anonymity.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Content red teaming probes the app dynamically for blind spots, multi-turn failures and subjective harms; define targeted vs open-ended objectives; use domain experts, AI experts and target end users with diversity; track acceptable response rate, refusal rate and turns-to-unsafe; annotators may be red teamers, independent third parties or LLM judges with human sampling; automated red teaming (e.g. PAIR, Crescendo-style) is an emerging complement.
who_tests: Developers/deployers, domain experts, independent annotators, automated tools

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (IMDA / AI Verify Foundation, published 30 May 2024; PDF file dated 19 June 2024)
clause_or_page: Trusted Development and Deployment dimension, 'Evaluation', p.14 (government-transparency sentence in 'Disclosure', p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: Benchmarking and red teaming are the two main evaluation approaches today but fall far short of a robust assessment (front-end focus, missing tools incl. dangerous-capability tests, poor comparability); the framework calls for a more comprehensive, systematic safety evaluation approach that could include a baseline set of required safety tests developed in consultation with policymakers; the adjacent Disclosure text says greater transparency to government will be needed for potentially high-risk models.

framework: Abu Dhabi Law No. (3) of 2024 establishing the AI and Advanced Technology Council
requirement_paraphrase: The Council sets the conditions, controls, standards and systems that must be observed in AI investment and research, and follows the performance and feasibility of AI-related policies. The law gives no explicit power to test AI systems.
what_is_tested: None directly (policies and standards-setting; performance of policies)

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.2(b), Annex A printed p.13 (current 10.3.2(b) would become 10.3.2(c))
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed: no one may use, operate or offer for commercial use a System that processes personal data unless the System has been tested for safety verification, including native regulatory and security design (in addition to human-defined purposes and design compliance with Reg. 10.3.1 and Commissioner audit, governance or certification requirements).
what_is_tested: Safety of the System, including regulatory and security design

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit self-assessment tool (Digital Dubai)
clause_or_page: Page sections 'What is the self-assessment tool for?' and 'What does it contain?'
requirement_paraphrase: Developer or operator organisations can self-assess an AI system's ethics level against Dubai's AI Ethics Guidelines across fairness, accountability, transparency and explainability, after classifying the system as non-significant, significant or critical; the tool reports gaps and suggests mitigations. Guidelines are recommended, not mandatory; the tool is in beta.
what_is_tested: AI system ethics level and gaps across four aspects

framework: Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles in Dubai
requirement_paraphrase: No modification, upgrade or update to features of the Autonomous Driving System may be made without prior RTA approval; RTA approves only after verifying the change will not affect performance or endanger lives or property.
what_is_tested: Changes to the Autonomous Driving System (pre-change verification)

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Vulnerability assessments should continue and system behaviour in unexpected situations, including dual-use cases, should be addressed through preventative measures.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Ethics > Safety, security and robustness (H3) > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Establish performance metrics measuring accuracy of outputs; test the system in a variety of scenarios including extreme or rare events; implement red teaming and record behaviour under unexpected or anomalous scenarios.
who_tests: Not specified (delivery team or red team is an inference)

framework: UK Frontier AI Safety Commitments (AI Seoul Summit 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatory organisations commit to assess risks of frontier models across the lifecycle, including before deployment, considering results from internal and external evaluations such as independent third-party evaluators and home governments.
what_is_tested: Frontier model risk assessment before deployment
who_tests: Signatory developers; independent evaluators/home governments as appropriate

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Verify the architecture can monitor outputs and recover from errors when security anomalies are detected; verify the system handles inappropriate, malicious or illegal queries properly; regularly evaluate vulnerabilities to circumvention of safety measures.

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (3 April 2025) - federal agency use of AI [added beyond assigned scope]
clause_or_page: Scope section; Appendix s.1(a) p.4 and s.1(c) p.5 (national security systems exclusion); s.4 intro (pp.13-14)
requirement_paraphrase: Memo is directed to heads of all executive departments and agencies, including independent regulatory agencies; the s.4(a)-(b) high-impact practices do not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community, and AI in national security systems is not covered.
